question: Six days after undergoing a thoracic endovascular aortic repair following a high-speed motorcycle accident, a 29-year-old woman develops a fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Serum studies show a sodium concentration of 129 mEq/L. An x-ray of the chest shows a left-sided pleural effusion. Thoracentesis is performed and shows milky white fluid in the pleural space that remains uniform after centrifugation. A culture of the pleural fluid shows no organisms. Further analysis of the fluid would most likely show which of the following?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Thoracic endovascular aortic repair" -> "possible injury to lymphatic vessels" -> "chylothorax" -> "milky white pleural fluid" -> "high triglycerides" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Pleural effusion" -> "milky white fluid" -> "uniform after centrifugation" -> "likely chylothorax" -> "high triglycerides" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Left-sided pleural effusion" -> "thoracentesis performed" -> "milky white fluid" -> "no organisms in culture" -> "suggests non-infectious etiology" -> "high triglycerides" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Post-surgical complications" -> "fever, cough, shortness of breath" -> "pleural effusion" -> "milky white fluid" -> "high triglycerides" -> 70%
analysis: The pleural fluid is described as milky white and remains uniform after centrifugation, which is characteristic of chylothorax. This condition is often associated with high triglyceride levels in the pleural fluid due to lymphatic obstruction or injury, especially following trauma such as a motorcycle accident. Therefore, further analysis of the fluid would most likely show high triglycerides.
